flows.name: brainstorm-cards
flows.description: Interactive brainstorm-with-vitamins: turns a rough idea into one or more Agentic Cards inside .backlog/.

flows.name: auto-optimizer
flows.description: Continuously profiles and upgrades algorithmic complexity and performance in an infinite loop.

steps.prompt: Profile the codebase for performance hotspots and algorithmic bottlenecks
Identify functions with suboptimal Big-O complexity
Generate optimized implementations with benchmarks
Run tests to verify correctness after optimization
Commit changes and loop to the next hotspot

flows.name: auto-reducer
flows.description: Continuously refactors and simplifies the codebase to reduce complexity and remove bloat.

steps.prompt: Scan the codebase for dead code, duplication, and unnecessary complexity
Identify the highest-impact simplification opportunity
Refactor the code while preserving external behavior
Run the full test suite to verify no regressions
Commit changes and loop to the next reduction target

flows.name: auto-visual-fixer
flows.description: Continuously audits and fixes UI/UX accessibility and layout issues without altering brand identity.

steps.prompt: Audit the UI for accessibility violations and layout inconsistencies
Prioritize issues by severity (WCAG compliance first)
Apply targeted CSS/component fixes without altering business logic
Verify fixes visually and with accessibility tooling
Commit changes and loop to the next UI issue

flows.name: auto-architect
flows.description: Continuously analyzes the project to autonomously generate and manage finite Agentic Cards in the backlog.

steps.prompt: Analyze project structure, dependencies, and architectural patterns
Identify areas needing refactoring, modularization, or cleanup
Generate finite Agent Sessions as backlog tasks for each improvement
Prioritize tasks by impact and dependency order
Continuously monitor for new architectural drift and create new tasks

flows.name: auto-optimizer-finite
flows.description: Executes a single, targeted algorithmic or performance optimization task from the backlog and terminates.

steps.prompt: Read the assigned optimization task from the backlog
Profile the target code section for performance metrics
Implement the optimization with benchmarks
Run tests to validate correctness
Mark the backlog item as complete and terminate

flows.name: auto-reducer-finite
flows.description: Executes a single, targeted refactoring or code reduction task from the backlog and terminates.

steps.prompt: Read the assigned reduction task from the backlog
Analyze the target code for safe simplification opportunities
Refactor and remove unnecessary complexity
Run tests to ensure no regressions
Mark the backlog item as complete and terminate

flows.name: auto-visual-fixer-finite
flows.description: Executes a single UI/UX accessibility or layout fix from the backlog and terminates.

steps.prompt: Read the assigned UI/UX fix from the backlog
Inspect the affected component for layout and accessibility issues
Apply the targeted fix preserving design consistency
Validate the fix with visual and a11y checks
Mark the backlog item as complete and terminate

flows.name: auto-feature-engineer
flows.description: Continuously consumes the backlog to build new features, write tests, and commit them sequentially in an infinite loop.

steps.prompt: Pull the next feature task from the backlog queue
Design the implementation approach and identify affected files
Write the feature code with proper type safety and error handling
Create or update tests covering the new functionality
Commit changes and loop to the next backlog feature

flows.name: auto-feature-engineer-finite
flows.description: Executes a single, targeted feature implementation or architectural addition from the backlog and terminates.

steps.prompt: Read the assigned feature task from the backlog
Plan implementation approach and identify dependencies
Build the feature with tests and documentation
Run the full test suite to verify integration
Mark the backlog item as complete and terminate

flows.name: auto-refiner
flows.description: Continuously analyzes and re-architects an existing codebase toward premium, production-grade quality through relentless functional (never cosmetic) upgrades.

steps.prompt: Analyze the project structure and inventory existing features
Autonomously generate a prioritized functional improvement backlog
Engineer real behavioral upgrades (not cosmetic) for the top item
Validate the improvement and log results to results.tsv
Commit changes and loop to the next backlog item

flows.name: auto-saas-cost-reducer
flows.description: Continuously audits infrastructure-as-code, paid API usage, and deployment configs to reduce cloud/SaaS spend without degrading the user experience.

steps.prompt: Analyze IaC, deployment configs, and paid API usage
Inventory expensive operations and generate a prioritized FinOps backlog
Implement the highest-impact cost reduction without degrading UX
Validate savings and log to finops_results.tsv
Commit changes and loop to the next cost-saving target

roles.name: frontend-engineer
roles.description: Expert in UI/UX, reactive frameworks, DOM manipulation, advanced CSS, and browser APIs.

roles.name: backend-engineer
roles.description: Specialist in APIs, databases, server logic, and infrastructure architecture.

roles.name: devops-engineer
roles.description: Expert in CI/CD pipelines, containerization, cloud infrastructure, and automation.

roles.name: security-researcher
roles.description: Paranoid focus on AppSec, cryptography, vulnerability auditing, and prevention of injections.

roles.name: software-architect
roles.description: High-level systems design expert focusing on microservices, SOLID principles, scalability, and fault tolerance.

roles.name: data-scientist
roles.description: Master of Python, mathematics, data pipelines, and AI/ML frameworks.

roles.name: qa-engineer
roles.description: Obsessed with edge cases, end-to-end testing, continuous integration, and TDD/BDD practices.

roles.name: product-manager
roles.description: Focuses on user and business value, writing user stories, and defining success metrics.

roles.name: technical-writer
roles.description: Transforms complex code and architectural decisions into clear documentation and API specifications.

roles.name: full-stack-engineer
roles.description: Pragmatic end-to-end engineer who ships complete vertical slices: UI, API, and data model as one coherent feature.

roles.name: design-engineer
roles.description: Hybrid expert in UX/UI, frontend architecture, and Developer Experience (DX). Crafts minimalist, highly functional interfaces.

roles.name: ai-engineer
roles.description: Builds LLM-powered applications: prompts, agent loops, RAG, structured outputs, and eval-gated changes.

roles.name: mobile-engineer
roles.description: Ships native-feeling mobile apps with React Native/Expo or Flutter: offline-first, 60fps, store-ready.

roles.name: incident-responder
roles.description: Triages live failures with log forensics, change correlation, and rollbacks; mitigate first, root-cause second, postmortem always.

mods.name: strict-linting
mods.description: Enforces strict linting rules and automatically fixes all warnings.

mods.name: test-driven
mods.description: Requires writing and presenting unit tests before implementing any core logic.

requiredArtifacts.description: At least one test file must exist for the change (TDD red before green)

mods.name: zero-dependencies
mods.description: Forbids adding new third-party dependencies; solutions use native language features and standard libraries.

mods.name: security-hardened
mods.description: Applies extreme sanitization, uses parameterized queries, and flags potential security risks.

mods.name: verbose-comments
mods.description: Forces detailed explanatory comments for every block of logic, function, and complex variable.

mods.name: dry-run
mods.description: Prevents final code generation, outputting only pseudocode, flowcharts, and step-by-step explanations.

mods.name: legacy-compat
mods.description: Prioritizes safe patches and backward compatibility over massive refactors or modern syntax.

mods.name: extreme-performance
mods.description: Prioritizes raw execution speed and lowest Big-O complexity, even at the cost of readability.

mods.name: a11y-enforcer
mods.description: Forces all generated UI elements to include ARIA labels, focus management, and pass WCAG AAA standards.

mods.name: output-budget
mods.description: Optimizes for the smallest correct artifact and fewest tokens; enforces surgical edits over full rewrites.

mods.name: regression-sentinel
mods.description: Brownfield guard: read before write, preserve public contracts, limit blast radius, and prove prior features survive.

mods.name: spec-adherence
mods.description: Treats the specification as law: extracts every rule into a checklist, implements each, and self-verifies adherence.

mods.name: systematic-debug
mods.description: Hypothesis-driven debugging: reproduce, isolate, hypothesize, and verify with an exact file:line — no blind loops.

mods.name: self-review
mods.description: Runs a finalization self-review against the objective and prior team artifacts before declaring a task complete.

mods.name: edge-case-coverage
mods.description: Forces robust handling of edge cases (nulls, boundaries, overflow, invalid types) with real general logic instead of happy-path or hardcoded answers.

mods.name: i18n-ready
mods.description: Externalizes every user-facing string, enforces ICU message format and locale-aware date, number, and currency formatting.

mods.name: structured-data
mods.description: Emits valid Schema.org JSON-LD structured data for every page type (Article, Product, FAQ, Breadcrumb, Organization).

mods.name: seo-meta
mods.description: Enforces a complete semantic document head: titles, meta description, canonical URLs, Open Graph and Twitter cards, sitemap and robots awareness.

mods.name: web-vitals
mods.description: Holds rendering to Core Web Vitals budgets (LCP, INP, CLS) via lazy-loading, code-splitting, and layout-stable markup.

mods.name: auth-guarded
mods.description: Requires authentication and authorization (RBAC) on every route, endpoint, and server action; default-deny access with explicit grants.

mods.name: responsive-design
mods.description: Forces mobile-first, fluid layouts with container queries and relative units; forbids fixed pixel widths that break on resize.

mods.name: dark-mode
mods.description: Requires tokenized light/dark/system theming via CSS custom properties and prefers-color-scheme; forbids hardcoded colors.

mods.name: form-validation
mods.description: Requires accessible client and server validation with typed schemas, inline error messaging tied to inputs, and no trust in client input.

mods.name: ds-tailwind
mods.description: Pins all styling to Tailwind CSS utility classes and design tokens; no ad-hoc CSS or competing styling systems.

mods.name: ds-shadcn
mods.description: Pins all UI to the shadcn/ui design language and Radix primitives composed with Tailwind.

mods.name: error-ux
mods.description: Requires explicit loading, empty, and error states with retry paths on every remote-data surface; no swallowed rejections.

mods.name: observability-ready
mods.description: Enforces structured correlation-id logging, golden-signal metrics, and spans on every new endpoint; forbids console.log and unobservable code.

mods.name: api-contract-first
mods.description: The API contract (OpenAPI/schema) is written and validated before implementation; types, clients, and validation derive from it.

mods.name: docs-sync
mods.description: Every change updates the README, API references, and changelog entries it invalidates — stale docs are defects.

mods.name: privacy-guard
mods.description: GDPR-grade data handling: classify fields, minimize collection, keep PII out of logs, and preserve deletion/export paths.

mods.name: conventional-commits
mods.description: Atomic commits in Conventional Commits format with why-focused bodies and clean, reviewable history.

mods.name: explain-to-me
mods.description: Plain-language pedagogy in the conversation: defines jargon, uses project-anchored analogies, and recaps every change for non-expert builders.

mods.name: db-migrations-safe
mods.description: Reversible, expand-contract schema migrations with idempotent batched backfills and zero destructive changes at deploy time.

steps.name: scaffold-structure
steps.description: Lays down the folder and file skeleton for a feature or module, matching project conventions, before any logic is written.

steps.name: write-failing-tests
steps.description: Specifies desired behavior as executable tests that fail before any implementation exists (TDD red).

steps.name: implement-to-green
steps.description: Writes the smallest correct implementation needed to make failing tests pass (TDD green).

steps.name: review-diff
steps.description: Reviews a change against a quality rubric and reports concrete findings without rewriting the code.

steps.name: refactor-safely
steps.description: Improves the internal structure of existing code without changing its observable behavior.

steps.name: landing-page
steps.description: Builds a single conversion-focused landing page (hero, value props, social proof, CTA) as one artifact, matching the project's design system.

steps.name: auth-pages
steps.description: Builds the authentication UI surface (login, signup, and password-reset screens) wired to the project's auth provider.
